land.text: the Nationalist zone of 1936, taken from the Republic by the rising of 17 to 19 July 1936: Spanish Morocco, the Canary and Balearic islands, Old Castile, León, Galicia, Seville and Cádiz (Spanish Civil War page)

predecessors.note: The rising is the birth of the faction: infobox dates '17 July 1936 – 1 April 1939'.

land.text: the whole of Spain after the Nationalist victory, declared by Franco on 1 April 1939

successors.note: The Cliopatria row ends in 1938; the ledger carries the 1939 conquests, and the Francoist Spain row (this group) is the same regime from 1 April 1939.

capitals.name: Salamanca
capitals.note: Francoist Spain page footnote: 'Salamanca served as the de facto Nationalist capital' and 'administrative functions were moved to Burgos'; the page gives no years for either, so the span is the whole war.

rulers.name: Francisco Franco
rulers.title: Caudillo (supreme leader)
rulers.note: Spanish Civil War page: 'Francisco Franco was appointed supreme leader on 1 October 1936.' Before that date a military junta led the rising; the pages opened do not name its head.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 1936-1937 plus Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands, which the rising held from July 1936; the 1937 northern conquests are added by the ledger. Spanish Guinea, Ifni, Cape Juby and the Sahara are left out because no page opened dates them

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws one 207,657 km2 shape for 1936-1937 that covers the Old Castile, León, Galicia, Navarre, Seville and Cádiz zone of the coup (gazetteer overlay: Cantabria only 14 percent, no Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa or Asturias, none of Málaga or Granada) but leaves out the overseas land the page says the rebels held at once, Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands. The page gives the share of population (11 of 25 million, 44 percent), not an area; the shape is 41 percent of the 506,537 km2 of Kingdom of Spain's 1976 shape, which is in line. The north of Spain is added by the 1937 events, not by this shape.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1938 shape plus Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands

keyframe_review.note: The 1938 shape (338,687 km2; gazetteer overlay: Bizkaia 89, Cantabria 95, Asturias 90, Castellón 82, Teruel 98, Lérida 36, Tarragona 23 percent) fits the front after the Aragon Offensive: 'By April 15 the Nationalists had reached the Mediterranean sea at Vinaròs' and 'Lleida and Gandesa fell on April'. It again omits Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands. Plausible rather than measured: the page gives no area.

correction.text: the whole of Spain and its colonies as Cliopatria draws Francoist Spain in 1939; the Nationalists held it from the end of March to 1 April 1939

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Nationalist shape for 1939 and draws the whole of Spain as Francoist Spain from that year. The Nationalists took Catalonia ('much of Catalonia was captured in 1938 and 1939') and then the rest, and 'Franco entered the capital and declared victory on 1 April 1939'. The shape is the Francoist Spain shape of 1939 and holds for the months before 1 April; the Francoist row takes the full year colour.

region.text: the zone held after the coup: Morocco, the Canaries, Old Castile, León, Galicia, Seville, Cádiz

ledger.note: 1936: the generals rise against the Republic. 'the men in the Morocco protectorate were to rise up at 05:00 on 18 July' and mainland Spain a day later; 'The result of the coup was a nationalist area of control containing 11 million of Spain's population of 25 million.' The Nationalist faction page dates the faction 17 July 1936 to 1 April 1939.

region.text: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco

ledger.note: 18 July 1936: the Army of Africa rises. Spanish Morocco page: the Civil War 'began in Spanish Morocco' with 'an uprising of the Spanish Army of Africa stationed there'; Spanish Civil War page: 'Control over Spanish Morocco was all but certain.'

region.text: the Canary Islands and the Balearic Islands

ledger.note: 1936: Franco and Goded take the islands. 'Goded and Franco immediately took control of the islands to which they were assigned' (Franco the Canary Islands, Goded the Balearic Islands). The page does not say which Balearic islands; Menorca is not named.

region.text: the Cliopatria 1936 shape: the Nationalist mainland zone

ledger.note: July to October 1936: the rebel zone on the mainland. The rebels took 'Old Castile, León and Galicia, which fell quickly', Seville ('Queipo de Llano secured Seville for the rebels') and Cádiz; the Republicans kept Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, most of the east coast, most of Asturias and Cantabria and part of the Basque Country.

region.text: the northern coast: Biscay, Gipuzkoa, Cantabria and Asturias

ledger.note: 31 March 1937: the Nationalist offensive in the north opens. The theatre 'occurred in northern Spain from 31 March to 21 October 1937'.
19 June 1937: Bilbao falls. The Nationalists 'entered the city on 19 June, completing their conquest of the Biscay and the Basque Country.'

region.text: Santander and almost all of Cantabria

ledger.note: 26 August 1937: Santander falls. 'On 26 August, the Italians occupied the city of Santander'; by 1 September 'the Nationalists had occupied almost all of Cantabria'. The page's introduction says Santander fell 'in September'; the body gives 26 August.

region.text: Gijón and Asturias, the last of the northern zone

ledger.note: 21 October 1937: Gijón falls and the north is lost. 'By 21 October, the Nationalists had occupied Gijón and completed the conquest of the northern zone' after breaking the Republican front on 14 October; the Republic lost the Army of the North and '36% of Spanish industrial production'.

region.text: the northern coast, now wholly Nationalist

ledger.note: 21 October 1937: the northern campaign ends with the whole coast in Nationalist hands.

region.text: the rest of the growth between the 1936 and 1938 shapes: Andalusia, Extremadura and the Madrid sector (Málaga, Badajoz, Toledo, Córdoba, Guadalajara and the like)

ledger.note: 1938: the rest of the growth of the Cliopatria shape between 1936 and 1938, in Andalusia, Extremadura and the Madrid sector (gazetteer overlay of the 1938 against the 1936-37 shape: Málaga 92 against under 2 percent, Huelva 95 against under 2, Toledo 64 against under 2, Badajoz 77 against 4, Madrid 66 against 9, Córdoba 61 against 16). Page silent: none of the pages opened dates these captures (the Spanish Civil War page gives only 'capturing most of Spain's northern coastline in 1937' and the Battle of Ebro without a date), so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Aragon east of the front, the Lleida and Gandesa sector and the Maestrazgo coast: the Aragon Offensive zone

ledger.note: 7 March 1938: the Aragon Offensive begins. 'The offensive, which ran from March 7, 1938, to April 19, 1938'; it 'punched a huge hole in the front, created a salient from Belchite to Caspe to Alcañiz'; 'Caspe fell on March 17'.

region.text: the 1938 Cliopatria shape in Aragon, the Lleida and Gandesa sector and the coast around Vinaròs and Castellón, minus the 1936 shape and the north: the ground of the Aragon Offensive, 7 March to 19 April 1938

ledger.note: 15 April 1938: the Nationalists reach the Mediterranean at Vinaròs. 'By April 15 the Nationalists had reached the Mediterranean sea at Vinaròs'; 'Lleida and Gandesa fell on April'; they 'held 40 miles (64 km) of the Mediterranean coastline' by 19 April. The page does not say the Republican zone was split; the region is the Cliopatria delta restricted to Aragon, Catalonia and Valencia.
19 April 1938: the offensive is 'for all intents and purposes concluded'.

1939: Catalonia. The page says 'After much of Catalonia was captured in 1938 and 1939 and Madrid was cut off from Barcelona'; it gives no day for Barcelona. The Catalonia offensive itself is not on any page opened.

region.text: Spain proper in 1939 without the 1938 Nationalist shape and Catalonia: Madrid, Valencia, Murcia, Alicante and the rest of the Republican remainder

ledger.note: 1 April 1939: Franco declares victory. 'Franco entered the capital and declared victory on 1 April 1939'; infobox of the faction 'Nationalist victory: 1 April 1939'. The page gives no date for Madrid's surrender or the Casado coup (the Republic dossier dates the central and south-eastern collapse to March 1939).

region.text: the whole of Spain and its colonies

ledger.note: 1 April 1939: the Nationalist state becomes Francoist Spain. 'Franco entered the capital and declared victory on 1 April 1939'; the Francoist Spain row of Cliopatria draws the whole of Spain from 1939.

wars.name: Spanish Civil War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: 'Franco entered the capital and declared victory on 1 April 1939'.
wars.note: Nationalist faction page: 'More than 13,000 Moroccan troops were airlifted' with German Ju 52s and 'an expeditionary force of 35,000 Italians' was in Spain by January 1937. Dates of the Catalan, Madrid and Levante campaigns are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: War in the North
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Bilbao 19 June, Santander 26 August, Gijón 21 October 1937.

wars.name: Aragon Offensive
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the sea is reached at Vinaròs on 15 April 1938 and the offensive is concluded on 19 April.

certainty.note: Civil-war front lines, moved by campaigns and not fixed by any treaty; the northern provinces and the Aragon front are dated by the pages, the other lines by Cliopatria's shapes only.

sources.title: Nationalist faction (Spanish Civil War)

notes:
Page budget (1-2) exceeded: seven pages were opened because the 1936 and 1938 shapes and the 1937 to 1939 conquests could only be dated from the campaign pages; the Spanish Civil War page gave few months.

Cliopatria problems: (1) the two shapes (1936-1937 and 1938) cover mainland Spain only and leave out Spanish Morocco and the Canary Islands, which were Nationalist from July 1936; the Second Spanish Republic row of Cliopatria therefore still carries them in 1936-1938 (the Republic dossier by eu-21-c already marks them as lost in July 1936). (2) The 1936-1937 shape is the end-of-1936 front; it is one shape for two years, so the north (Bizkaia 19 June, Cantabria 26 August, Asturias 21 October 1937) is added by the ledger, not by a keyframe. (3) Spanish Guinea, Ifni, Cape Juby and the Sahara are inside Cliopatria's Francoist Spain 1939 shape; no page opened says when they passed to the Nationalists, so they appear in no event of this dossier and a gap-filler should date them (Spanish Guinea page opened for francoist-spain is silent on 1936). (4) The Catalonia offensive (December 1938 to February 1939), Málaga (1937), the Madrid and Levante fronts and the Balearic split (Menorca stayed Republican) are not on any page opened; a gap-filler should open Catalonia Offensive and Battle of Málaga. (5) The Nationalists end on 1 April 1939 here to match the Second Spanish Republic dossier, whose 1939 losses and dissolution name this dossier and francoist-spain; the 1939 keyframe reuses the Francoist 1939 shape.

Capital: the Francoist Spain page footnote names Salamanca as de facto capital and Burgos for administration without years. Rulers: Franco from 1 October 1936 only; the junta before that is not named on the pages opened.
Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer already has: Spanish Morocco, Canary Islands, Catalonia. 'Baleares' is the Natural Earth admin-1 name.
